# SPAG Adversarial-vs-Non-Adversarial Self-Play: Full Experiment Design (design-only; nothing herein was run)

## 0. Framing and labeling rules
Question: does SPAG's adversarial recipe (SFT on GPT-4 Adversarial-Taboo demos → adversarial self-play) produce larger downstream reasoning gains than non-adversarial game recipes (20-Question, Guess-My-City)? Every number-like statement below is either a **design choice** (a knob we set) or flagged **unverified recollection** (e.g., base model, benchmark list). No value in this document is a source fact unless marked so. No experiment described here has been executed.

## 1. Arms (7 total)
| Arm | Recipe | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | Base model, no training | Anchor; defines "pre" for every gain |
| A1 | SFT on GPT-4 **Taboo** demos, no self-play | Isolates distillation-vs-game in the adversarial arm |
| A2 | SFT(Taboo) → adversarial self-play (**SPAG**) | Treatment |
| A3 | SFT(20Q demos) → 20Q self-play | Non-adversarial comparator 1 |
| A4 | SFT(GMC demos) → GMC self-play | Non-adversarial comparator 2 |
| **D1** | SFT on **generic instruction text**, token-matched, no self-play | **Decoy/active control** (Req 3): separates "any chat-shaped training keeps the model sharp" from game-specific signal. Cheap: one SFT run, public instruction corpus (e.g., a pinned Dolly/OpenAssistant-style mix — choice is a design choice). |
| A5 (optional) | Self-play(Taboo) **without** SFT | SFT-necessity decomposition; drop first if compute is tight |

Arms A2–A4 run **both** phases with per-arm paired, game-matched demo sets (approved resolution of open question (a) — **design choice**, not paper fact). Judge in self-play: same base architecture, frozen copy (SPAG uses a separate Llama-2-7B judge — **unverified recollection**). Base model: Llama-2-7B — **unverified recollection, parameterized below**.

## 2. Fixed across arms A1–A4, D1
Same base checkpoint and tokenizer; SFT token budget matched by truncating/padding episode counts (target: equal total tokens ±2%); same optimizer (AdamW), LR schedule (cosine, peak LR a fixed shared value — design choice), epochs=1 over the token budget (design choice); self-play: equal **episode counts** and equal **gradient-update counts** across A2–A4; dialogue turns, episode length, and win-condition remain **native per game** (approved resolution of (b)); 3 seeds (13, 42, 7); eval: identical harness, prompts, shot counts, greedy decoding (temp=0), one 80GB-class GPU per eval job.

## 3. Game-difficulty normalization and "trained enough" rule (Req 1)
**Fixed external referee:** one frozen copy of the **base** A0 model per game role (attacker-side and judge-side where the game has two roles), never gradient-updated, never in any training set. Every 20% of the self-play episode budget, each arm plays N=500 games (design choice) vs the frozen referee; record win-rate, episode length, taboo-rule violation rate.

**Pre-registered "trained enough for fair comparison" rule** — an arm qualifies iff:
1. **Learned:** final referee win-rate ≥ 55% (above the ~50% chance baseline for role-symmetric games; per-game chance baselines precomputed by rule analysis — Taboo judge role, 20Q guesser, GMC guesser have asymmetric baselines, computed at design time by random-play simulations of rule engines, **not run here**);
2. **Plateaued:** |win-rate slope| over the last two 20%-segments < 2 points per segment (still-climbing → under-trained);
3. **Not dead-flat:** win-rate improved by > 1 point over the arm's own first segment (flat → game not learned; arm flagged and its comparison declared inconclusive, not silently dropped).
A still-climbing arm at budget exhaustion triggers **one** pre-registered budget extension applied to **all** self-play arms simultaneously (compute parity preserved); if still climbing after the extension, the arm is reported as under-trained and the primary comparison carries that caveat.

## 4. Demo-corpus descriptor set (Req 2) — report, don't optimize
For each of the 4 demo corpora (Taboo, 20Q, GMC, D1-instruct), publish before any result: total tokens, mean/median tokens per episode, mean turns per episode, mean tokens per turn, and a **coarse reasoning-chain length per turn** = mean count of reasoning-connective tokens ("because, so, therefore, wait, since, then, must be, check") per turn via fixed wordlist — deliberately dumb and reproducible. Plus episode-diversity: distinct-word ratio and distinct-topic/taboo-word count. **No arm is reweighted to equalize these.** They appear as Table 1 in any report so a reader can see data-quality differences between arms before self-play begins.

## 5. Primary outcome — pinned first (Req 4)
**Headline number:** `G(arm, seed) = (1/|B|) Σ_{b∈B} (acc_post − acc_base) / (1 − acc_base)` — normalized pre→post gain, averaged over benchmark suite **B**.
**Headline comparison:** `H(seed) = G(A2,seed) − [ (G(A3,seed)+G(A4,seed))/2 ]`. **H is the single primary quantity.** Everything else — A1, D1, A5, per-benchmark breakdowns, in-game curves — is **secondary**, labeled as such in the pre-registration file.
**B is a named parameter:** `BENCH_SUITE = {GSM8K, MATH, CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, LogiQA}` — **unverified recollection of SPAG's suite; must be confirmed against the source or replaced before pre-registration; final list freezes before any checkpoint is scored.**
**Answer-extraction spec (pre-registered, versioned, deterministic):** greedy decode, fixed stop sequences; per-benchmark extractor — GSM8K: last number after "####" else last numeral in final line; MATH: content of last `\boxed{}`, string-normalized (LaTeX canonicalized: strip spaces/`\,`, fraction and unit forms canonicalized); MC (CommonsenseQA/ARC/LogiQA): first occurrence of a bare option letter A–D, else full-option-string match after lowercasing and article/punctuation stripping. A frozen 30-case unit-test suite per extractor must pass **before** scoring; extraction failures count as wrong. Scorer hash recorded in the pre-registration.

## 6. Seeds, statistics, divergence (Req 5)
**What 3 seeds supports:** direction and rough magnitude of H, and seed-consistency (sign of H across seeds). **What it does not support:** any precise effect size, any per-benchmark inferential claim, any "significant difference" phrasing. n=3 gives a minimum two-sided permutation p of ~0.25 for the sign-flip test — so **we do not run or report a p-value for H**; we report per-seed H values, mean H, and an item-level paired bootstrap CI (resample benchmark *items*, 10k resamples, seeds averaged) explicitly labeled as reflecting item variance, **not** training-run variance. Pre-registered claim tiers: "positive in 3/3 seeds" > "2/3" > "1/3 or mixed → inconclusive at this n."
**Divergence rule (pre-registered):** a seed is excluded from the primary mean only if it hits a **mechanical** trigger fixed in advance — loss > 10× median within-run loss, gradient-norm NaN, or degenerate self-play (violation rate > 90% or win-rate < 10% for 2 consecutive eval blocks). Excluded seeds are listed with trigger, and the **3-seed and 2-seed H means are both reported**. No post-hoc seed judgment calls.

## 7. Compute and feasibility (Req 6)
**Estimates** (transparent, order-of-magnitude, from assumed budgets since source figures are unknown: ~10k demo episodes ≈ 10–20M SFT tokens; 7B full fine-tune; ~2 self-play rounds × ~5k episodes with generation-dominated cost):
- SFT phase (A1–A4, D1): **~50–150 A100-80GB-hours per arm** (training + checkpoint eval).
- Self-play phase (A2–A4): **~300–800 A100-hours per arm** — dominated by rollout generation and the referee eval blocks; this is the dominant cost line.
- D1 is the cheap arm (SFT only). A0 is eval-only (~5 GPU-h).
- **Total campaign (7 arms × 3 seeds, minus A0 replication): roughly 4k–9k A100-80GB-hours.** These are planning bands, not measurements.
**External dependency not satisfiable here:** GPT-4 demo generation requires a pinned GPT-4 endpoint (network is disabled) — the four demo corpora + referee rule engines + base checkpoint are **input artifacts** to be obtained from the paper's released data if public, else regenerated externally and frozen with published hashes.

**Can be validated in this environment:** per-arm YAML/JSON config schemas (dry-run parse + constraint checks, e.g., token-budget equality); the answer-extraction unit-test suite against hand-written placeholder model outputs (stdlib Python only — verified the analysis-logic pattern runs here); demo-descriptor computation code against synthetic placeholder corpora; bootstrap/gain computation on hand-typed placeholder vectors (done as a smoke test — placeholder numbers only, no meaning).
**Cannot be done here:** any training, any inference (no torch, no GPU access, no weights), any benchmark scoring (no datasets), GPT-4 demo generation (no network), dependency installation (no network), and therefore **any execution of this protocol or production of any real number in it.**

## 8. Residual open items (not resolvable by me)
Whether SPAG's source actually paired the SFT phase across games (our paired design is a **choice** that de-confounds; if the paper didn't, our result extends rather than replicates it); exact BENCH_SUITE; judge freezing; native episode counts in the source. All flagged in the pre-registration file as "unknown — design choice made."

context.question: Does the adversarial game setup used in SPAG, which includes imitation learning of GPT-4 followed by self-play on game episodes (specifically via the adversarial Taboo game), provide superior reasoning improvements compared to non-adversarial setups like 20-Question and Guess-My-City?
